title: Competing Russia-Ukraine Ceasefires Collapse Immediately
detail: Both Russia's and Ukraine's unilateral ceasefires collapsed almost immediately after taking effect, with each side blaming the other for violations. Russia's ceasefire for May 8–9 began but Russian drone and missile attacks continued, while Ukraine struck targets in Crimea. Ukrainian forces carried out a strike against a Project 22800 Karakurt-class small missile ship at Russia's naval base in Kaspiysk, Dagestan, on the night of May 7. A large electrical substation in occupied Crimea caught fire overnight May 7–8 following a Ukrainian drone attack. The failures of both unilateral ceasefires set the stage for US President Trump to broker a three-way agreement.

media.caption: Both unilateral ceasefires collapse as each side blames the other for violations

title: Ukraine Strikes Russian Warship at Kaspiysk Naval Base
detail: Ukrainian Defense Forces carried out a strike against a Project 22800 Karakurt-class small missile ship at Russia's naval base in Kaspiysk, Dagestan — a Caspian Sea port approximately 1,500 km from Ukraine. The Karakurt-class ships are capable of launching Kalibr cruise missiles against Ukrainian targets. The strike demonstrated Ukraine's continued campaign to degrade Russia's long-range strike platforms, even during the nominal ceasefire period. Separately, a Russian military unit in Simferopol, Crimea was also reportedly struck.

media.caption: Ukraine strikes Russian Karakurt-class vessel at Kaspiysk naval base, Dagestan
